title: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) · Paper 4 — original full-length mock (calculator)
subject: cambridge-igcse-mathematics-0580
instructions: Original full-length practice: 24 questions, 100 marks. This is not an official or endorsed Cambridge examination. Answer every question and all parts. Show your reasoning and calculations in the working canvas beneath each question; add pages when needed. A scientific calculator is required; algebraic and graphical calculators are not permitted. Retain unrounded values during calculations. Unless a question specifies otherwise, give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures and angles in degrees to one decimal place. Use the calculator value of π or 3.142. Formula facts are attached to every question. Draw and label your own axes where requested; one grid square may represent the scale stated in the question. Use straight ruled lines and smooth curves as appropriate. Dimensions stated in a question are exact unless described as rounded. There is no separate reading period.

resources.label: Extended formula facts
resources.text:
Mathematical formula facts — independently typeset for this practice paper
Triangle: area = bh/2 (b is the base, h the perpendicular height).
Circle: area = πr²; circumference = 2πr (r is the radius).
Cylinder: curved surface area = 2πrh; volume = πr²h.
Cone: curved surface area = πrl; volume = πr²h/3 (l is slant height; h is perpendicular height).
Sphere: surface area = 4πr²; volume = 4πr³/3.
Prism: volume = cross-sectional area × length.
Pyramid: volume = base area × perpendicular height / 3.
If ax² + bx + c = 0 and a ≠ 0: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a).
In a triangle with sides a, b, c opposite angles A, B, C:
a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C;
a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A;
area = ab sin C / 2.

questions.label: Question 1
questions.prompt: Calculate √(18.7² + 26.4²)/0.0735. Give your answer to three significant figures. [2]

questions.label: Question 2
questions.prompt: A car travels a distance recorded as 128 km to the nearest kilometre, in a time recorded as 1.6 hours to the nearest 0.1 hour. Calculate the upper bound of its average speed. [3]

questions.label: Question 3
questions.prompt: An invoice total of $763.20 includes a sales tax of 6%. Find the price before tax and the amount of tax. [3]

questions.label: Question 4
questions.prompt: A machine costs $18500 when new and loses 13% of its value each year. Calculate its value after four years and the percentage of its original value that remains. [3]

questions.label: Question 5
questions.prompt: The intensity I of a signal is inversely proportional to the square of the distance d metres from its source. I = 48 when d = 5. Find an equation connecting I and d, then find d when I = 7.5. [3]

questions.label: Question 6
questions.prompt: Make x the subject of y = (3x − 4)/(x + 2). State the value of y for which your rearranged expression is undefined. [3]

questions.label: Question 7
questions.prompt: Solve 3x² − 5x − 11 = 0, giving both answers to three significant figures. [3]

questions.label: Question 8
questions.prompt: Find all points where the line y = 2x + 1 meets the circle x² + y² = 25. [4]

questions.label: Question 9
questions.prompt:
A(−3,5) and B(7,1) are endpoints of a segment.
(a) Find the midpoint of AB. [1]
(b) Find the gradient of AB. [1]
(c) Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB in the form y = mx + c. [2]

questions.label: Question 10
questions.prompt:
A quadratic sequence begins 6, 15, 28, 45.
(a) Find the nth term. [3]
(b) Find the first term greater than 500. State its position and value. [1]

questions.label: Question 11
questions.prompt:
Two mathematically similar containers have volumes 640 cm³ and 2160 cm³. The smaller has height 12 cm and total surface area 352 cm².
(a) Find the larger container's height. [2]
(b) Find its total surface area. [2]

questions.label: Question 12
questions.prompt:
In triangle ABC, AB = 8.6 cm, AC = 12.3 cm and angle BAC = 57°.
(a) Calculate BC. [2]
(b) Calculate the area of ABC. [2]

questions.label: Question 13
questions.prompt:
A boat travels 12 km due east from P to Q, then 7 km due north from Q to R.
(a) Calculate the distance PR. [2]
(b) Calculate the bearing of R from P, to one decimal place. [2]

questions.label: Question 14
questions.prompt:
A cuboid has length 9 cm, width 6 cm and height 4 cm.
(a) Calculate the length of its space diagonal. [2]
(b) Calculate the angle the space diagonal makes with the horizontal rectangular base. [2]

questions.label: Question 15
questions.prompt: A circle has radius 10 cm. A chord subtends an angle of 74° at the centre. Calculate the area of the smaller segment cut off by the chord. [4]

questions.label: Question 16
questions.prompt:
A solid metal cone has radius 4.5 cm and perpendicular height 12 cm. It is melted and recast without loss into a cylinder of radius 3 cm.
(a) Calculate the cone's volume. [2]
(b) Calculate the height of the cylinder. [2]
(c) Calculate the slant height of the original cone. [1]

questions.label: Question 17
questions.prompt:
A train accelerates uniformly from rest to 24 m/s in 40 s, continues at 24 m/s for 150 s, then decelerates uniformly to rest in 60 s.
(a) Draw a labelled speed–time graph for the journey. [2]
(b) Calculate its initial acceleration. [1]
(c) Calculate the total distance travelled. [2]

questions.label: Question 18
questions.prompt:
A delivery company's parcel masses m kg are:
0 < m ≤ 2: frequency 12
2 < m ≤ 5: frequency 24
5 < m ≤ 10: frequency 20
10 < m ≤ 20: frequency 4
(a) Estimate the mean mass. [3]
(b) Calculate all four frequency densities for a histogram. [2]

questions.label: Question 19
questions.prompt:
The masses m grams of 80 apples are recorded cumulatively:
m ≤ 80: 0; m ≤ 100: 8; m ≤ 120: 28; m ≤ 140: 60; m ≤ 160: 76; m ≤ 180: 80.
(a) Draw a cumulative-frequency graph. [2]
(b) Estimate the median mass. [1]
(c) Estimate the interquartile range. [2]

questions.label: Question 20
questions.prompt:
A box contains 5 working and 3 faulty lamps. Two lamps are selected at random without replacement.
(a) Find the probability that exactly one is faulty. [3]
(b) There are 140 identical boxes. The same selection process is independently repeated once for each box. Estimate how many selections contain two working lamps. [2]

questions.label: Question 21
questions.prompt:
Triangle A has vertices (1,2), (4,2), (1,4). It is reflected in the y-axis, then translated by the column vector (5, −1).
(a) Draw and label the final image on a grid. [3]
(b) Give a single mapping rule (x,y) ↦ (…,…) for the combined transformation. [1]
(c) Is the final image congruent to A? Give a reason. [1]

questions.label: Question 22
questions.prompt:
For y = x³ − 4x + 1:
(a) Calculate y for x = −2.5, −2, −1.5, −1, 0, 1, 1.5, 2. [2]
(b) Draw the curve for −2.5 ≤ x ≤ 2, using at least two grid squares per x unit and a suitable uniform y scale. [2]
(c) Use your graph to estimate all three roots of x³ − 4x + 1 = 0 to one decimal place. [2]

questions.label: Question 23
questions.prompt:
A rectangular pen is built against a straight wall, so fencing is required on only three sides. There are 48 m of fencing. Let x metres be the length of each side perpendicular to the wall.
(a) Show that the area A is 48x − 2x², and give the range of physically possible x values for a non-zero pen. [2]
(b) Use differentiation to find the maximum possible area. [3]
(c) State the length of the side parallel to the wall at this maximum. [1]

questions.label: Question 24
questions.prompt:
A laboratory model predicts N = 750 × 1.08ᵗ bacteria after t hours.
(a) Find the predicted population after 12 hours, to the nearest whole bacterium. [2]
(b) Find the first whole hour when the predicted population exceeds 2000. Show values that justify your answer. [3]
(c) State one reason this model may be unreliable over a very long period. [1]
